title: Determinants of Survival After PDAC Resection: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis of Prognostic and Risk Factors
summary: While overall cancer mortality rates have declined over the past decade, pancreatic cancer–related mortality remains high, and it is predicted to become the third leading cause of cancer-related death by 2030. To date, complete surgical resection combined with systemic perioperative chemotherapy represents the only potentially curative treatment strategy, with five-year overall survival (OS) reaching up to 43% in highly selected cases. Survival outcomes after resection for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are influenced by a constellation of factors, including tumour location, tumour biology (e.g., margin status, nodal involvement, tumour size, and grade), the use and timing of neoadjuvant and adjuvant therapies, perioperative management, and patient-specific comorbidities. A comprehensive understanding of individual prognostic factors associated with recurrence and reduced overall survival, as well as the impact of postoperative morbidity on overall survival and recurrence, is therefore essential to optimize treatment strategies and tailor postoperative surveillance.

interventions.name: Evaluation of the preoperative and intraoperative factor affecting prognosis for patients who underwent upfront pancreatic resection for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma or after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
